status: Meets the Bench Standard bar on totals: it beats no skill on both models in every round (final round Haiku 62/64 and Opus 63/64 vs no skill 45/64 and 53/64), beats no skill on trap totals (final round 26/28 and 27/28 vs 20/28 and 23/28), passes lint, and the grader found no invented facts in any with-skill output in the final round. One exception to 'never worse on traps': on trap eval 4, final-round Opus scored 6/7 against no-skill Opus's 7/7, because its decision log put Jordan's name in 'Decided by' for requests that were declined. No comparison skill exists for this job, so there is no source comparison.
method: 9 evals (4 traps), expectations written before any run. Round 1 ran the skill and no skill on Haiku and Opus, each in a fresh headless agent, graded blind by a separate Opus grader that read only evals.json and the fixtures. Round 2 re-ran the revised skill on Haiku; round 3 re-ran it on Haiku and Opus. Both were graded blind the same way. No public comparison skill matches this job, so no comparison-skill config was run. Round 3 was interrupted by a network outage; the 12 unfinished runs were reset to clean fixtures and re-run from scratch before grading.
losses_and_open_issues: Round 3, Opus, eval 4 (trap): the decision log put Jordan Bell in 'Decided by' for his own declined requests; the reason column was correct. One point below no-skill Opus on that eval

Round 3, Haiku, eval 4 (trap): held back the approval state ('Priya must see v2') although Priya's and Hannah's conditional sign-offs were met by v2; the same over-caution shows unpenalised in evals 5 and 7, on both models. The skill's rule on when 'approved with changes' counts needs to be applied consistently
Round 3, Haiku, eval 3 (trap): reply over 250 words because it pasted the full newsletter after the user asked for 'the final version' (its own text was 212 words)
Round 1, Haiku, eval 8: asked whether Maria's written permission existed rather than suggesting getting it (fixed in 1.1.0)

Round 1, with skill: Haiku logged a decision as made by a name taken from outside the review (the test machine's user); Opus opened two replies with 'Using the editorial-review-cycle skill' and flagged a brand-confirmed fact as unsupported (fixed in 1.1.0, not seen in rounds 2-3)

Round 2, Haiku: extra copies of the version and packet in evals 7 and 8, one with a model-name suffix, most likely from an interrupted run overlapping its resume in the same folder (file rule added in 1.2.0; not seen in round 3)

Small slips noted by graders that no expectation caught: 'from $299' group rate shortened to '$299' (round 2, Haiku); an absolute run path listed in a reply (round 3, Haiku); a date-logic error about which approval route was faster (round 1, Haiku)

Without the skill: 7 of 36 runs overwrote the original instead of writing a new version; no-skill Opus added an unsourced 'under 60%' figure and called it well sourced, wrote placeholder or invented headlines in the contested spot (evals 2 and 9), and ran 600+ word replies; no-skill Haiku did nothing in eval 5, changed a product fact and converted American spelling in eval 6
No with-skill run in any round marked a piece approved without the required sign-offs, or added an unsupported reviewer statistic to a new version
